title: Finite cohomological dimension gives derived coproduct compatibility
statement: Let $u:U\to T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $A$ be a finite commutative coefficient ring. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(U_{\Et},A)$ and $D(T_{\Et},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with direct image $u_*$ and its higher right derived functors as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Suppose that $R^pu_*M=0$ for every etale $A$-module sheaf $M$ and every $p>c$, for a fixed integer $c\geq0$. Then the total right derived functor $Ru_*:D(U_{\Et},A)\to D(T_{\Et},A)$, with the natural derived comparison of [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex], preserves every set-indexed coproduct: for every family $(K_s)_{s\in S}$ in $D(U_{\Et},A)$, the canonical map $\bigoplus_{s\in S}Ru_*K_s\to Ru_*(\bigoplus_{s\in S}K_s)$ induced by the coprojections is an isomorphism. No boundedness or constructibility condition is imposed on the $K_s$, and the empty family is included.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\Mod(U_{\Et},A)$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod(T_{\Et},A)$. These categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian], and have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The functor $F=u_*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. A finite ring has positive characteristic $N$ (take $N=1$ for the zero ring), so every underlying abelian sheaf of an $A$-module is killed by $N$. For a family $(M_s)$, its sum is the filtered colimit of $M_J=\bigoplus_{s\in J}M_s$ over finite subsets $J\subseteq S$, including the empty subset: a compatible family of maps from the $M_J$ is precisely a family of maps from all the $M_s$. Forgetting coefficients preserves these colimits and is faithful and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. The canonical natural derived coefficient comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison] is invertible and compatible with the degree-zero direct-image identity. Evaluate it on $M[0]$ and take degree-$p$ cohomology. Exact forgetting preserves kernels, images and their quotients, so it identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^pF(M)$ with the abelian higher direct image naturally in $M$. Thus the square between the module and abelian filtered-colimit comparison maps commutes: on the leg indexed by $J$, both composites are the higher direct image of the map $M_J\to\bigoplus_s M_s$ under this natural identification; equality on all colimit legs implies equality of the two maps. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] to the filtered diagram of these torsion sheaves; $u$ has exactly its qcqs hypotheses. Finite sums commute with $R^pF$: take the finite sum of injective resolutions; it is exact and its terms are injective, since extension of a map into a finite biproduct of injectives is performed in each component. Additivity of $F$ preserves this finite biproduct, and kernels and images of its componentwise differential are the finite sums of the kernels and images. Therefore $R^pF(M_J)=\bigoplus_{s\in J}R^pF(M_s)$, with the identifications respecting the inclusions of finite subsets. The filtered comparison gives, after forgetting, the canonical isomorphism $\bigoplus_s R^pF(M_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^pF(\bigoplus_s M_s)$ for every $p\geq0$. These maps are $A$-linear. Faithful exact forgetting reflects their invertibility: its vanishing kernels and cokernels imply zero module kernels and cokernels. Thus these are isomorphisms of module sheaves. The natural identification $R^0F\cong F$ is [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. In particular the $p=0$ case says $F$ commutes with arbitrary sums of sheaves.

proof.text: Let $(K_s)_{s\in S}$ be any family in $D(\mathcal A)$. Choose complex representatives $C_s$ and apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] in the Grothendieck category $\mathcal A$ to obtain quasi-isomorphisms $C_s\to I_s$, where every $I_s$ is K-injective and every term $I_s^r$ is injective. Let $L=\bigoplus_s I_s$ be the termwise sum, with differential induced by the differentials of the $I_s$. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], $Q_{\mathcal A}L$ with the localized coprojections is the coproduct of the $K_s$. This result applies to arbitrary unbounded complexes and every set in the chosen indexing universe; no common lower bound on the $K_s$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F11, lemma-finite-cd-mod-n-direct-sums, proof of (1), adapted from Z/nZ to finite constant A using the stated module cohomological-dimension hypothesis

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], $R^pF(I_s^r)=0$ for every $p>0$, since $I_s^r$ is injective and $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives. Step 1 now gives $R^pF(L^r)\cong\bigoplus_sR^pF(I_s^r)=0$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$ and $p>0$. Thus both $I_s$ and $L$ have $F$-acyclic terms. Apply [lem-kun-finite-cd-acyclic-complex] to $F$ with $d=c$: its source is Grothendieck, its target abelian, $F$ additive and left exact, and the required uniform vanishing is precisely the hypothesis of the item. It supplies the unbounded $RF=Ru_*$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_{I_s}:Q_{\mathcal B}(F I_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}I_s)$ and $\alpha_L:Q_{\mathcal B}(F L)\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}L)$. For each coprojection $\iota_s:I_s\to L$, naturality gives $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}\iota_s)\circ\alpha_{I_s}=\alpha_L\circ Q_{\mathcal B}(F\iota_s)$. Hence these identifications preserve the coprojection maps, not just the objects.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, (1)-(2), with n=c+1; injective vanishing is Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors (3)

proof.text: Use the $p=0$ comparison of Step 1 on $(I_s^r)_s$ in every degree $r$. It gives a canonical isomorphism $\beta^r:\bigoplus_s F(I_s^r)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(L^r)$. Each component restricted to the $s$th summand is $F(\iota_s^r)$. The chain-map equation for $\iota_s$ implies $F(d_L^r)F(\iota_s^r)=F(\iota_s^{r+1})F(d_{I_s}^r)$. Maps out of a coproduct are determined by these restrictions, so the $\beta^r$ commute with differentials and form a complex isomorphism $\beta:\bigoplus_s FI_s\xrightarrow{\sim}FL$. The target category $\mathcal B$ is Grothendieck by Step 1, so [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] says $Q_{\mathcal B}(\bigoplus_s FI_s)$, with the localized termwise legs, is the derived coproduct of the $Q_{\mathcal B}(FI_s)$. Localizing $\beta$ gives an isomorphism to $Q_{\mathcal B}(FL)$. Under the comparison isomorphisms of Step 3, its restriction to each summand is $RF$ of that summand's coprojection. It is therefore exactly the canonical map $\bigoplus_s Ru_*K_s\to Ru_*(\bigoplus_sK_s)$, by the coproduct universal property, and is invertible. For the empty family the same construction uses the zero complex and the degreewise zero-to-zero comparison, so it proves that case too.
